CPHI trade show: what experienced exhibitors understand that Pharma brands often miss

06.09.26Exhibits, Trends
Written by David Atkinson, Exhibits Account Director at Iventions

I’ve attended CPHI Trade Show for many years, and one thing I’ve noticed is how much the exhibition continues to evolve. Every year, exhibitors place greater importance on the look and feel of their stands, while visitors expect more than a simple product showcase.

The brands that leave a lasting impression aren’t necessarily the ones with the biggest spaces. They’re the ones that create environments people want to spend time in. In an industry built on trust, quality and long-term relationships, standing out requires much more than visibility alone.

What people misunderstand about CPHI?

 

One of the biggest misconceptions about CPHI is that success comes from simply being seen. Visibility certainly matters, but credibility matters just as much.

 

The exhibitors people remember are often those who create welcoming, professional spaces that encourage interaction. Interactive elements, LED screens, comfortable seating areas and thoughtful hospitality all play a role. Visitors remember the stands where they felt comfortable, where conversations flowed naturally and where the experience reflected the quality of the brand behind it.

 

First-time exhibitors sometimes make the mistake of creating spaces that feel too clinical. While cleanliness and professionalism are important in the pharmaceutical industry, visitors increasingly respond to stands that feel more inviting. Introducing colour, natural elements and warmer design features can bring life to a space without compromising professionalism.

 

The most trustworthy stands tend to share similar characteristics. They feature quality finishes, dedicated meeting areas, strong branding, clear messaging and well-integrated technology. Above all, they feel considered. Every detail contributes to the overall impression.

 

Why CPHI works differently from other trade shows?

 

At technology events, visitors are often focused on discovering new products and innovations. At CPHI, many attendees arrive with a clear commercial objective. They want to build relationships, expand their network and identify opportunities that can support future business growth.

 

The pharmaceutical industry is inherently global. A product developed in one market can have relevance across many others, which is why CPHI continues attracting decision-makers from around the world. For exhibitors, the event provides an opportunity to establish partnerships that may help them enter new regions, strengthen their supply chain or accelerate market expansion.

 

That environment creates a certain level of pressure. Many companies offer similar products and services, which means exhibitors need to communicate their value clearly. Successful exhibitors understand that it’s not enough to have a great product. You also need the right people on the stand, a clear message and an environment that encourages meaningful conversations.

 

Long-term relationships are especially important in pharma. Many of the discussions that begin at CPHI continue long after the exhibition closes, often developing into partnerships that support future product launches and business growth.

How attention works differently in pharma exhibitions?

 

Pharma is a professional, precise and highly regulated environment. Stands that feel overly busy or visually overwhelming can quickly lose credibility. Visitors are looking for clarity. They want to understand what a company does, what products it offers and why it might be a valuable partner.

 

This is why good stand design is often less about creating noise and more about creating confidence. White continues to play an important role because it reflects cleanliness and professionalism, while carefully introduced brand colours help create personality without distracting from the message.

 

Comfort is another factor that shouldn’t be underestimated. Trade shows are demanding, and visitors appreciate having somewhere to sit, have a coffee and engage in conversation. Comfortable seating, engaging product demonstrations and clear navigation all contribute to keeping people on a stand for longer.

 

I’ve also seen smaller stands outperform larger competitors. Larger spaces naturally allow for more meetings and product displays, but size alone doesn’t guarantee success. The key is using the space effectively and ensuring every area serves a purpose.

What experienced exhibitors understand?

 

Experienced exhibitors understand that successful exhibitions begin long before the event opens.

 

For a project of this scale, I always recommend starting six to nine months in advance. There are many stages involved, including design development, internal approvals, material selection, graphics production and stand manufacturing. Giving yourself enough time allows every element to be properly considered.

 

Many of the issues that create stress during an exhibition stem from details that were overlooked during planning. Product demonstrations aren’t ready. Video content arrives late. Equipment responsibilities haven’t been clearly assigned. Refreshments haven’t been organised. Individually these may seem minor, but collectively they can affect the overall experience.

 

From my perspective, a well-run stand feels effortless. Visitors are welcomed properly, products are easy to explore, meetings run smoothly and the entire environment feels organised and professional. Most visitors never see the planning behind that experience, but they certainly notice when it’s missing.

How Iventions support exhibitors at CPHI?

 

One of the things our clients appreciate most is the guidance we provide throughout the entire exhibition process.

 

The pharmaceutical industry places a strong emphasis on precision, and those expectations naturally extend to exhibition projects. Clients expect everything to be delivered professionally on time and to a high standard.

 

At Iventions, we help guide exhibitors through every stage of the journey. We understand venue regulations, production requirements and the countless details that need to be coordinated behind the scenes. Our experience allows us to anticipate challenges early and ensure projects progress smoothly.

 

Effortless execution isn’t effortless for the project team. It requires careful planning, coordination and attention to detail. Our role is to manage that complexity so our clients can focus on their objectives and make the most of their time at the exhibition.

 

Planning your presence at CPHI trade show 2026?

 

Successful exhibition experiences don’t start when the doors open. They start months earlier through careful planning, clear objectives and the right partnerships.

 

The exhibitors who achieve the best results are usually the ones who give themselves the time and support needed to get every stage right. Because at CPHI Trade Show, preparation isn’t just part of the process, it’s often what makes the difference between being present and being remembered.
